title: Sesame Ginger Tofu Bowls
seoTitle: Sesame Ginger Tofu Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Crisped tofu, edamame, and vegetables over rice with a sesame-ginger sauce
subtitle: Crisped tofu, edamame, and vegetables over rice with a sesame-ginger sauce
description: Pressed tofu is pan-crisped until golden, then served over rice with edamame, shredded carrots, and cucumber in a sesame-ginger sauce. It is the hall's first fully vegetarian high-protein bowl option.

steps.title: Press the tofu
steps.instruction: Wrap tofu blocks in paper towel and press under a heavy pan for at least 15 minutes to remove excess water. Dry tofu is the difference between crisp edges and a soggy pan.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice, bring it with water to a boil in a lidded pot, then reduce to low and simmer 18 minutes. Rest 10 minutes off heat, then fluff.

steps.title: Cube and coat the tofu
steps.instruction: Cut pressed tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and toss gently with cornstarch until lightly coated. The cornstarch is what creates the crisp shell in the pan.

steps.title: Crisp the tofu
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Add tofu in a single layer and let it sit undisturbed 3 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp on most sides, about 10 minutes total.

steps.title: Mix the sesame-ginger sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, ginger, and sesame oil in a small bowl until the honey dissolves. Toss half of it with the warm tofu right in the pan.

steps.title: Warm the edamame
steps.instruction: Steam or microwave edamame with a splash of water 3–4 minutes until hot. Toss with a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Layer rice, edamame, carrots, and cucumber in each bowl, top with crisped tofu, and drizzle the remaining sauce over the top. Finish with sesame seeds if using.

steps.title: Hold for a delayed line
steps.instruction: If service is delayed, hold tofu uncovered on a rack over a sheet pan in a 200°F oven so the crust stays crisp instead of steaming soft under a lid. Target oven/smoker temperature: 200°F.

proTips: Prep tip: Do not skip pressing the tofu — wet tofu will not crisp no matter how hot the pan is.
Rookie tip: Let tofu sit undisturbed in the pan; flipping it too early tears off the crust.
Add sriracha or chili crisp on the side for crews who want heat.
Double the sauce batch and keep extra on hand — this dish tends to run out of sauce first.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Store tofu separately from rice and re-crisp it in a dry skillet rather than the microwave.
Cool rice and vegetables in shallow containers within two hours of cooking.
Leftover tofu and vegetables work well cold, tossed with extra sauce, as a next-day lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The sauce and crisp texture do the convincing — most crews are surprised how filling and flavorful a vegetarian night can be, and it gives anyone avoiding meat a real seat at the table.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: press and marinate tofu up to a day ahead; sauce holds 5 days. Storage: keep tofu, rice, and vegetables separate up to 4 days. Reheating: reheat tofu in a dry skillet to re-crisp rather than the microwave, which turns it soft.
substitutions: Use tempeh instead of tofu for a firmer, nuttier bite.
Use brown rice or quinoa instead of jasmine rice.
Use tamari instead of soy sauce for a gluten-free version.

adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos.
